newsitem.title: USA: IMM CURRENCY FUTURES END BUSY TRADE WITH BIG GAINS.
newsitem.headline: IMM CURRENCY FUTURES END BUSY TRADE WITH BIG GAINS.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended with hefty gains but off day's peaks, with afternoon trade winding down from a quick early clip.

Traders decided the morning's breakneck-speed rally, which at one point hoisted Septemer marks to an intraday gain of more than $0.0100, was due to technicals and the stunning whipsaw lower that jolted U.S. Treasuries and stocks.

"I think it was technical, and I think it was the (U.S.) stock and bond markets. They were unbelievable," one IMM floor broker of reasons for the abrupt morning rally in currencies. "It was a wild morning, and then everything hit a wall."
"When the bonds started to back off" is when currencies rallied in earnest, said another floor broker.

Currencies, many of which had posted losses in overight electronic trading, had returned to small gains by the pit's opening. They initially trimmed those gains as U.S. Treasuries spike higher when U.S. economic data showed few signs of worrisome inflation pressures.

Produer prices last month fell 0.1 percent overall and in the core rate. Economists had expected 0.1-percent gains in each. U.S. retail sales rose 0.6 percent versus forecasts for up 0.7 percent. It rose 0.5 percent minus autos, as forecast.
But the gain-cutting proved shortlived as futures respected support zones, including $0.5418 or 1.85 dollar/mark, and currency futures soon snapped upward again.

September marks and Swiss francs rallied on heavy volume as shorts scrambled for cover, with sizable fund buying seen in both pits. September marks triggered big buystops, including near $0.5450. But the contract faltered at the next key level, $0.5480 or 1.8290 spot.
"We only came through that by two ticks," added the second broker. He said a rise above that level would clear the path for a mark rise toward $0.5500.

They also said the mark regained ground on sentiment that the Bundesbank might be more biased to tightening credit to guard against inflationary pressures. Fueling the quick pop up was a London newspaper article that said Germany and France might delay European economic and monetary union if Britain agreed to join at the outset.
German officials later dismissed the newspaper article as "pure speculation."
Several brokers said they doubted the currency futures rally would persist, with several characterizing the move up as technically corrective in nature.
"I'm not too worried about it (dollar's drop)," said the second floor broker.
Volume was robust on the morning rise but quickly faded.

Before midday, mark futures had racked up volume of roughly 34,000 contracts. After Europe shut, order flows dried up, and only an additional 5,000 or so mark futures changed hands during the final two and one-half hours of pit trading.

September yen rose $0.000064 to $0.008687, marks rose $0.0087 to $0.5461, Swiss rose $0.0066 to $0.6643, pound up $0.0066 at $1.5820, Can dollar flat at $0.7191, Aussie dollar rose $0.0054 to $0.7444, Mex peso added $0.000150 to $0.126800.
